result:
F-DG5-147 is fixed and its regression test failed before the fix and passes after it, in en and ar. While running the existing specs, the same overflow turned up in one more place, and I fixed that too. Everything is left uncommitted in `/home/user/wt/dg5-fe-aa1`, and the DG4 historical validator exits 0 at both start and end.

**Fix** (`apps/web/src/styles/app.css`, CSS only, no component changes)
- **Lines 380–398:** page-header titles and subtitles, breadcrumb items, card titles and dialog titles now wrap long unbroken text (`overflow-wrap: anywhere`), as D-178 decided. The header row's title block is also allowed to shrink (`min-inline-size: 0`).
- **Lines 1587–1589:** entries in `.entry-list` lists wrap the same way. My first run of the existing specs found this: `p5-reflow-axe` failed in chromium-ar on `/playbook/launch-plan` and `/playbook/health-check` (806 px of horizontal scroll at 390 px). Their transformation picker lists names as links, and my spec's 120-character name was now in the database. en missed it only because that spec ran before my data existed.

**Regression test** (`apps/web/e2e/p5-title-reflow.spec.ts`)
- **What it does:** qa's R5-TITLE probe, now with assertions. Per language it creates synthetic transformations whose name and benefit title hold a 120-character word, the 46-character token and ordinary text. It opens the T14 benefit page, the transformation overview and the picker at 390 × 900, 320 × 900 and 1280 × 900 with 200 % text.
- **What it asserts:**
  - the page does not scroll sideways (`scrollWidth - innerWidth <= 1`);
  - every heading, breadcrumb and picker link carrying the title stays inside the viewport;
  - ordinary titles still render on one line at 1280 px.
- **Before the fix:** 2 failed, exit 1, with 24 overflow cases whose values match qa's numbers exactly (for example 44 / 114 / 113 px on the benefit page and 183 / 253 / 415 px on the overview for the 46-character token).
- **Before the picker fix only:** 2 failed, picker cases only.
- **After both fixes:** 0 px of sideways scroll in every case. Screenshots of my spec only are in `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG5/T-DG5-FE-AA1-evidence/shots/{en,ar}/`.

**Checks on the final tree**

| Check | Exit | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `pnpm -r typecheck` | 0 | |
| `pnpm -r build` | 0 | |
| `pnpm lint` | 0 | |
| prettier check | 0 | |
| `pnpm openapi:lint` | 0 | |
| `unit-web`, locale unset | 0 | 1713/1713 |
| `unit-web`, C.UTF-8 | 0 | 1713/1713 |
| 4 e2e specs (mine, `p5-form-tables-reflow`, `p5-reflow-axe`, `p5-forms`), locale unset | 0 | 14/14 |
| Same 4 specs, C.UTF-8 | 0 | 14/14 |

Each e2e run covers chromium-en and chromium-ar. The handback explains every earlier non-zero exit: the intended before-fix runs, a first lint failure because my spec used `parseFloat` (now `Number`), and the first e2e run's picker failure. The repository-wide test, integration and full e2e runs were **not run** (D-164).

**Notes for you**
- **Shared test data:** my spec leaves transformations with very long names in the shared e2e database. If the full-suite run then shows overflow on another screen that lists names, that is a real product defect of the same kind, not a test bug.
- **Unchanged and unmeasured:** three title containers on the Define, Design and Gates screens (`.outcome-card__title`, `.tom-box__title`, `.gate-card__title`) may hold user text and still don't wrap. They are outside D-178's scope; a follow-up could add the same rule.
- **Nothing else needed:** no contract, schema or dependency change, no ADR made untrue, and no user-facing text changed.

Everything is in `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG5/`; open `T-DG5-FE-AA1-frontend-ux-engineer.md` first, and the logs are in `T-DG5-FE-AA1-evidence/`.
